test_title: PYST 47: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What does the Constitution of India stipulate regarding the composition of the Election Commission of India (ECI)?

options.text: It is constitutionally fixed as a single-member body headed by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) only.
It must always be a three-member body (one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners).
It must include one Election Commissioner from each major state to ensure federal balance
It may be single or multi-member; initially, there was only a Chief Election Commissioner until 1989.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It may be single or multi-member; initially, there was only a Chief Election Commissioner until 1989**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution of India under Article 324 establishes the Election Commission of India (ECI) and grants it authority over the conduct of elections in India.
 
• Article 324 does not specify a fixed composition for the Election Commission; it gives the President of India the discretion to determine whether the ECI is a single-member or multi-member body.
 
• Initially, the ECI was a single-member body with only a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) until 1989.
 
• In 1989, the ECI became a multi-member body with the appointment of two Election Commissioners in addition to the CEC. Since then, it has functioned as a three-member body in most instances.
 
• The President has the authority to appoint Election Commissioners, and the composition of the Election Commission may vary over time as per requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution of India.

It is responsible for conducting free and fair elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

 
• The ECI operates independently and is vested with powers to ensure impartiality and transparency in the electoral process.
